provenance.notes: Headless command capture of the reference engine; one fresh engine instance per case (gap G10, edge weight for subdivision surfaces). Original provenance carried this same source/method pair with prose in extra fields ("gap", "notes") where the house schema (tools/local/fixture_gen/provenance.py) wants a fixed {schema, source, reference, method, captured_utc} shape -- reference/schema/captured_utc added here to satisfy provenance_check.py; source and method are verbatim from the original capture.

rig.cage: unit cube, 1 segment per axis, corners at (+/-0.5, +/-0.5, +/-0.5)
rig.creased_loop: the four edges of the +Y face (used by the 'loop' cases)
rig.output: refined control positions at the stated level, NOT limit positions: level 1 of the un-creased cube puts the edge point at (0, 0.375, 0.375) = (v0+v1+f0+f1)/4

law.weight_units: the stored per-edge scalar; the editor UI shows it as a percentage, 1.0 == 100%
law.infinite_threshold: sharpness >= 10 is the usual 'infinitely sharp' convention, so UI 100% is exactly the infinite-crease point
law.per_level_rule: uniform crease subdivision: a child edge inherits sharpness = parent - 1, floored at 0
law.fractional_rule: for residual sharpness s in [0,1] the refined position is exactly lerp(smooth_rule, sharp_rule, s) -- measured off-line residual < 1.1e-8 at every level
law.negative_weights: clamped to 0 by the Catmull-Clark evaluator (stored verbatim, no effect on geometry)
law.above_one: saturated; not separable from a clamp at 10 below subdivision level 10
law.boundary: an open-mesh boundary edge is unconditionally infinitely sharp and IGNORES the per-edge weight; a boundary vertex uses the crease rule (1/8, 6/8, 1/8) by default
law.storage: sparse per-edge scalar map, dimension 1, edge-domain; set is ABSOLUTE (not additive); 0.0 is stored as a value and behaves as no crease

readouts.single_edge_blend_note: blend_t at level L is only a valid readout of the RESIDUAL sharpness when every earlier level was saturated, i.e. weight >= (L-1)/10. Rows below that (level 2 with weight < 0.1, level 3 with weight < 0.2) are kept for completeness and read < 0 because the coarser levels differ too; they are not counterexamples to the law.

units.evidence: select-edges-by-weight with range 0.2..0.4 selects an edge set to 0.3 and range 20..40 selects nothing

boundary_cases.case: open box, weight 0.05 on a BOUNDARY edge
open box, weight 0.05 on a boundary edge, rule 'crease'
open box, weight 0.05 on an INTERIOR edge with only ONE end on a boundary vertex

falsifiers: level 1, weight 0.05 -> edge point other than (0, 0.4375, 0.4375)
any geometry response to a negative weight
level 2 saturated at weight 0.1 (would mean no per-level decrement)

rejected_candidates.law: sharpness = 10*weight, crease re-applied undecremented per level

rejected_candidates.falsified_by: level 1 blends are exactly 0.2/0.5/0.8 at weights 0.02/0.05/0.08 - dead linear
